title: Decide often, fail small
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: How many failures does it take for your ego to knock?
Jose said that you can make a decision and interpret things in your favor, you can be comfortable being uncomfortable, and comfortable adapting continually.
He said that from a probability standpoint, if you are making decisions all the time, even wrong ones, you will eventually make the right one and you will learn.

Jose described two mindsets in a business owner: one that wants to grow, take risks and decide, and another that has not felt the power to decide because of the responsibility of being the custodian of the business.
Jose said that there is no need for shame: it is only feedback, only adjustments. He asked how long it takes before your ego knocks on the door: three failures, four, seven?

He said that the first part is identifying how you manage your thoughts, then identifying other people's thoughts and limiting beliefs, and then more. He said happiness is discipline: you have the choice to wake up and call it the most extraordinary day.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a decision you are putting off.
Write the smallest version you can decide today.
Write how you will treat a wrong decision as feedback.
Write how many failures it takes for your ego to knock.
Write the discipline you will start with.

check.q: What did Jose say a wrong decision is?
What did Jose say happens if you decide all the time?
choices: You eventually decide right and learn

check.q: What did Jose say happiness is?

recap: Decide often. Treat mistakes as feedback. Keep the discipline.
